doctrine_constraint: Master prompt forbids any auth changes without explicit authorization. Output is findings + proposed fix scaffold only.

login_flows.step2_email: Backend mints magic-link token, emails link of shape /auth/verify.html?token=<magic>
login_flows.step5_use: performer-portal.html primarily relies on backend cookie session (fetch with credentials:'include') for /api/me + /api/member/profile. Falls back to URL ?session_token=<t> read on landing (performer-portal.html:146). Sends session_token as query param for /api/performer/offers (line 104).
login_flows.double_login_handling: If user clicks the same magic link twice, frontend has no UI affordance for 'already verified' vs 'consumed' — both surface as the generic error string returned by /auth/verify (auth/verify.html:48-49).
login_flows.old_token_reuse: Frontend never sets an exp / issuedAt, never compares times, never deletes the session_token on receipt of a 401 from any API. A copy-pasted (or browser-extension-leaked) session_token will keep being sent until the backend rejects it AND the user manually clears storage.
login_flows.session_persistence: Persists forever (until user 'Sign Out' nav link is clicked — but that link is just an anchor to /login.html and does not clear any storage; see P3-AUTH-FIND-1).

login_flows.step2_email_or_dev: Backend either emails the token or returns dev_token in the response when SMTP is unavailable.
login_flows.step3_persist: On request, login.html stores dev_token into localStorage immediately (login.html:129). Booker-portal and booker-dashboard only store it once 'useToken' is clicked (booker-portal.html:87, booker-dashboard.html:379).
login_flows.step4_use: All subsequent /api/booker/* + /api/booker/comics calls send X-Booker-Token header.
login_flows.double_login_handling: Submitting POST /api/booker/auth a second time always shows 'Token sent' or 'Token created' regardless of whether the previous token is still valid. UI does NOT warn the user the previous token has been (or may have been) revoked. After mint, three independent surfaces (login.html, booker-portal.html, booker-dashboard.html) each independently rewrite localStorage.booker_token, but each can store a DIFFERENT token if the user retries on a different page — last-writer-wins.
login_flows.old_token_reuse: No token version / fingerprint tracked. If backend rotates token on each /api/booker/auth call, the older one is silently stale in any tab still holding it. Frontend never compares.
login_flows.session_persistence: Persists until logout(). logout() is defined only in booker-dashboard.html:385 and is not wired to any UI element (the 'Sign Out' nav link is a plain anchor to /login.html). booker-portal.html has NO logout function at all.

login_flows.step3_use: Authorization: Bearer <token> header on POST/PATCH calls; URL query owner_token=<t> on GET /api/owner/shows.

Page does not redirect to /login.html on 401 in subsequent /api/owner/* calls — `api()` (show-runner.html:311) returns raw JSON without status inspection, so non-200 responses are interpreted as data and downstream code mis-renders.
login_flows.session_persistence: Forever. No logout function defined anywhere in show-runner.html.

findings.title: 'Sign Out' nav links do not clear any tokens
evidence: performer-portal.html:37 — Sign Out
booker-portal.html:37 — Sign Out
booker-dashboard.html:129 — Sign Out (NOT wired to logout() at line 385)
show-runner.html:65 — Sign Out
admin-*.html — all 'Sign Out' links are plain anchors to /login.html
partials/nav.shell.portal.html:8 + partials/nav.shell.admin.html:10
findings.explanation: Clicking 'Sign Out' navigates to /login.html but localStorage.{booker_token, pc_session_token, pc_owner_token, admin_token, pc_admin_secret} all remain intact. Next visit to any portal page silently re-authenticates with the supposedly-signed-out token. On a shared/borrowed device this is a credential leak.
findings.proposed_fix_description: Convert every 'Sign Out' nav anchor across portal + admin shells to a small inline button (or an anchor with onclick) that clears all localStorage keys whose names match a known token list ({booker_token, booker_email, pc_session_token, pc_auth_email, pc_owner_token, admin_token, pc_admin_secret, pending_claim_slug}) and THEN navigates to /login.html. Best done as a single shared helper in /assets/auth-helpers.js included by every portal/admin page.

findings.title: No 401 handler — stale tokens are never auto-cleared
evidence: booker-portal.html:85 — `api()` throws on !r.ok but never inspects status===401 / never removes booker_token
booker-dashboard.html:337-348 — same pattern, throws but does not clear
show-runner.html:311-315 — `api()` returns r.json() unconditionally, does not even check r.ok
performer-portal.html:98 — `api()` throws on !r.ok but never clears pc_session_token
admin-messages.html:94-95 — surfaces 'Auth failed' but does not localStorage.removeItem('admin_token')
findings.explanation: When the backend rotates / revokes a token (or when a magic link is consumed and the previous session_token is invalidated), the frontend continues to send the same token, hit 401, and surface a confusing 'Invalid token' or generic detail string. The user has to manually paste a new token or clear browser storage. This is the most likely root cause of ChatGPT's 'old token reuse' complaint.
findings.proposed_fix_description: Centralize each portal's `api()` helper into /assets/auth-helpers.js. On any 401/403 response: (a) localStorage.removeItem the role-specific token, (b) redirect to /login.html with ?reason=expired so login.html can surface a friendly banner. Wire this into 4 fetch sites: performer-portal, booker-portal, booker-dashboard, show-runner.

findings.title: Tokens transmitted in URL query strings — leak via Referer, server logs, browser history
evidence: show-runner.html:295 — GET /api/owner/shows?owner_token=<t>
show-runner.html:569-570 — accepts ?owner_token=<t> as auto-login source
admin-crm.html:192 — GET /api/imports/history?token=<t>
admin-crm.html:315-316 — accepts ?token=<t> auto-login
admin-messages.html:94 — GET /api/admin/messages?token=<t>
admin-events.html:108 — GET /api/admin/events/summary?token=<t>
performer-portal.html:104 — GET /api/performer/offers?token=<session_token>
auth/verify.html:45 — GET https://api.pariscomedy.com/auth/verify?token=<magic>
findings.explanation: Tokens in URLs end up in: browser history, the Referer header to any external resource loaded by the page (analytics, fonts, embeds), reverse-proxy access logs, browser extension reads, and screenshots. The magic-link case (auth/verify.html) is the canonical pattern and is acceptable because it's a one-shot consumed token. The persistent owner/admin/session tokens being sent as query params is unsafe.
findings.proposed_fix_description: Move all persistent-token reads to headers (Authorization: Bearer or X-Token). Backend will need to accept the header in addition to the query param during a transition window. For magic-link verify, keep the query param but recommend backend send {Referrer-Policy: no-referrer} on the verify response.

findings.title: Magic link 'double-login' surfaces only a generic backend error
evidence: auth/verify.html:44-50 — only differentiates {resp.ok, !resp.ok}, dumps data.detail as-is
auth/verify.html:69 — falls back to 'Request a new link' regardless of cause
findings.explanation: ChatGPT specifically called out 'magic link double-login'. Frontend has no special handling for the case where the same magic-link token is clicked twice (e.g., user clicks in email client, then again from history). Backend almost certainly returns 4xx with detail='already_used' or similar — but the frontend just shows the raw detail string. Worse: if the user IS already signed in (pc_session_token already set in this browser) and clicks an old link, we should detect that and redirect to /performer-portal.html with a 'You're already signed in' notice instead of showing an error.
findings.proposed_fix_description: In auth/verify.html, before calling /auth/verify, check `localStorage.getItem('pc_session_token')`. If present, attempt a HEAD/GET to /api/me with credentials:'include' first. If already signed in, redirect to /performer-portal.html with a banner. Otherwise hit /auth/verify. On a 4xx with detail matching /already.used|consumed|expired/, render a specific friendly state with a 'Send me a new link' button that POSTs /api/auth/request inline.

findings.title: login.html stores booker dev_token before user opts in
evidence: login.html:128-131 — `if(r.dev_token){ localStorage.setItem('booker_token',r.dev_token); ... }` runs on form submit, no user confirmation
findings.explanation: When the booker requests a token, login.html immediately writes the returned dev_token to localStorage. If the user is on a shared computer and walks away before clicking 'Open Booker Portal', the next user inherits the token. By contrast, booker-portal.html:87 only persists on explicit 'Load account' click — which is the correct UX.
findings.proposed_fix_description: In login.html submitLogin booker branch, DO NOT auto-persist booker_token. Instead, display it for copy, and only persist it when the user clicks 'Open Booker Portal' or 'Open Lineup Dashboard'.

findings.title: Show Runner auto-logins from URL query param without scrubbing it
evidence: show-runner.html:569-573 — reads ?owner_token from location.search, calls login(), never history.replaceState the token out of the URL
findings.explanation: Owner clicks a 'Manage your show' link containing ?owner_token=<t>. show-runner.html auto-logs in. The token remains in the URL bar, in browser history, and in the Referer of any external script load on the page. show-runner.html includes /assets/events.js (analytics) which will Referer-leak the token.
findings.proposed_fix_description: Right after auto-login parses the URL token, call `history.replaceState(null, '', location.pathname)` to strip the query string. Same pattern for admin-crm.html:315-316 and admin-events.html:171.

findings.title: No frontend exp / issuedAt — cannot pre-empt expired sessions
evidence: Every token-stash in localStorage is a bare opaque string — no JWT decode, no parallel '*_exp' key.
No code anywhere in the frontend parses token.split('.')[1] / atob() / compares Date.now().
findings.explanation: Frontend learns a token is dead only when a request fails. Pre-emptive refresh / proactive sign-out impossible. Combined with finding 2 (no 401 handler), this yields the 'old token reuse' user experience: token sits in storage, every API call fails opaquely.
findings.proposed_fix_description: When backend issues a token, also return `expires_at` (ISO timestamp). Frontend stores `{token, expires_at}` as JSON in a single key per role. Helper `getToken(role)` returns null if expires_at < now AND clears the entry. Requires backend coordination — note dependency.

findings.title: Dead localStorage write: pc_auth_email
evidence: auth/verify.html:55 — localStorage.setItem('pc_auth_email', data.email || '')
No corresponding getItem('pc_auth_email') in any frontend file.
findings.explanation: Orphan write that adds a PII (email) to localStorage without serving any feature. Harmless individually but accumulates session metadata over time and confuses 'clear all auth' helpers.
findings.proposed_fix_description: Either consume pc_auth_email in the portal display (replacing the /api/me round-trip for the email field), or delete the setItem.

findings.title: Comic claim flow never validates that pending_claim_slug came from the same session
evidence: performer-portal.html:191-205 — handleClaim() reads ?claim=<slug>, persists to localStorage, fires submitClaim immediately if signed in
performer-portal.html:228-236 — focus listener also auto-fires submitClaim from localStorage with no UI confirmation
findings.explanation: If user A starts a claim for slug-A, then user B signs in on the same browser without clearing storage, user B will silently auto-claim slug-A on window focus. Backend presumably has its own validation (only the rightful owner email can claim), but the UX is surprising.
findings.proposed_fix_description: Before auto-firing submitClaim, render an explicit confirmation banner with a 'Confirm claim of {slug}' button. Only fire on user click.

findings.title: Three independent token-storage surfaces — last-writer-wins, no canonical source
evidence: login.html, booker-portal.html, booker-dashboard.html each independently localStorage.setItem('booker_token', ...) with no coordination.
findings.explanation: A booker who has two tabs open can clobber a fresh token in tab A with a stale token in tab B if they retry /api/booker/auth in tab B. There is no token version field, no `storage` event listener, no single source of truth.
findings.proposed_fix_description: Centralize through /assets/auth-helpers.js with a single setBookerToken(t) that broadcasts via window.dispatchEvent('pc-auth-change') so other tabs reload. Add a 'storage' event listener that detects cross-tab logout and triggers re-render. Pairs with finding 1+2 fix.

summary.recommended_next_phase: P3.AUTH.2 — implement findings 1 + 2 + 3 + 5 + 6 (the no-backend-coordination subset). Findings 4 + 7 + 10 require backend coordination on token shape / verify error codes / token rotation and should be scoped as P3.AUTH.3. Finding 8 + 9 are quick polish — fold into P3.AUTH.2.

function setToken(role, token) — role-keyed setter; broadcasts pc-auth-change
function authFetch(path, opts, role) — wraps fetch; injects header; on 401 calls clearAllAuth + redirect to /login.html?reason=expired
function stripTokenFromURL() — history.replaceState w/o token query params

show-runner.html, admin-crm.html, admin-events.html — add stripTokenFromURL() after auto-login
